notes:
github_grabber.py (from github_grabber.go): class GithubGrabber with can_grab/grab; regexes compiled once with named groups, matched via walrus expressions in the same precedence order (file -> repo -> issue/pull, "pull" -> "pulls"); fetch -> _fetch using httpx.Client. Idiom calls: exceptions instead of (result, error) tuples; context.Context dropped (the client owns timeouts); IsCanGrab -> can_grab, Grab -> grab; NewGrabber dropped in favor of the constructor GithubGrabber(fallback, client=None); non-200 handled by response.raise_for_status() instead of Go's custom message. Missing grabber-package types defined minimally at top of module: Resource(address: str) and Result(body: bytes, content_type: str) as frozen dataclasses — Go's Reader + http.Header Parameters collapsed to body+content_type since Content-Type is the only parameter ever set; ContentGrabber as a typing.Protocol; FIREFOX_USER_AGENT constant stands in for client.Firefox.Value(). can_grab uses urlparse().hostname (lowercases/strips port; slightly more lenient than Go's exact Host compare, same observable behavior on all cases).

test_github_grabber.py (from github_grabber_test.go): pytest + @pytest.mark.parametrize. httpx.MockTransport replaces both Go test doubles: roundTripFunc (handler inspects/captures the request) and httptest.NewServer (status/body cases) — hermetic, no sockets. StubGrabber records grab() calls for the fallback test (asserts identity of the returned result). Two deliberate divergences from the Go tests: (1) the Go test asserted User-Agent "websearch/1.0" while its implementation sends client.Firefox — the port asserts the actual FIREFOX_USER_AGENT constant; (2) httpx always sends a default Accept: */*, so the raw-file case expects that rather than an empty header; the error cases use pytest.raises(httpx.HTTPStatusError / httpx.ConnectError).

tools_websearch.py (from tools_websearch.go): register(server, web_search_service) wires an async tool via the official Python MCP SDK — specifically mcp 2.x's MCPServer.tool(name=..., description=...) (FastMCP was renamed to MCPServer in SDK v2; I verified the import and decorator kwargs against the installed 2.x package). Go's reflection-derived OutputSchema maps to structured output inferred from the Output return annotation. Stand-ins defined for package-level Go symbols that live in sibling files: TOOL_NAME="web_search", AGENT_NAME, pydantic Input/SearchHit/Output, a WebSearchService Protocol with dataclass WebSearchInput/WebSearchResult/WebSearchOutput (url/title/snippet -> url/title/content mapping preserved, Limit hardcoded to 50), and description(agent, month_year) with plausible text. getMonthYear -> datetime.now().strftime("%b %Y").

Verification: ruff format ran successfully ("3 files left unchanged"); pytest 13/13 passed; a smoke test against the real mcp 2.x SDK confirmed registration (tool listed with a derived output_schema). uvx initially failed only because its default tool dir (~/.local/share/uv) is outside the sandbox's writable paths — redirecting UV_TOOL_DIR/UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR into /tmp/claude fixed it.
